newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-COLOMBIA CRUISE TO WIN OVER COSTA RICA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COLOMBIA CRUISE TO WIN OVER COSTA RICA.

text.p: Midfielder Neider Morrantes scored twice in his debut as Colombia beat Costa Rica 4-1 Monday to revive their chances of reaching the Copa America quarter-finals.
The 21-year-old, who plays for Medellin club Atletico Nacional, provided the firepower that Colombia have often been lacking as he struck twice 10 minutes apart in the opening quarter of the game.

Wilmer Cabrera added Colombia's third from a 62nd minute penalty and Victor Hugo Aristizabal completed the scoring in the 77th. In between, defender Mauricio Wright grabbed a consolation for Costa Rica to avoid a shutout.

Colombia, who have three points from two games in group C, have a fighting chance of making the quarter-finals, while Costa Rica with no points and nine goals against in their first appearance in the competition are virtually eliminated.
Morrantes opened his account in the 13th minute, slipping the ball past goalkeeper Hermidio Barrantes after a neat first time pass by Victor Pacheco wrongfooted the Costa Rica defence.
Ten minutes later, he scored with a powerful low drive after being found unmarked on the edge of the area.
Bad finishing has often been a problem for Colombia and although Morrantes' performance was encouraging, Hamilton Ricard, Victor Aristizabal, and Luis Zuleta (twice) all missed good chances.
Farid Mondragon was dropped after a series of crucial blunders but replacement Miguel Calero was badly at fault when he let Wright's weak header slip under his body at the near post.
Colombia coach Hernan Dario Gomez, like many of his peers, has rested his top players for the more important World Cup qualifiers and used the Copa America to test less experienced youngsters.
His team's play became more stylish as their confidence grew and in addition to Morrantes, Gomez should be pleased with the performances of Pacheco, Moreno and Aristizabal.
Costa Rica generally showed the same lethargy which led to a recent 1-0 defeat by Canada in a World Cup qualifier.

Colombia - 12-Miguel Calero, 4-Jose Santa, 5-Jorge Bermudez, 2-Ivan Cordoba, 16-Antonio Moreno, 13-Wilmer Cabrera, 6-Wilmer Perez, 20-Victor Pacheco (18-Victor Bonillo, 84), 22-Neider Morantes (10-Edison Mafla, 84), 17-Hamilton Ricard (7-Luis Zuleta, 46), 9-Victor Hugo Aristizabal

Costa Rica - 22-Hermidio Barrantes, 20-Geovani Jara, 4- Ronald Gonzalez, 19-Mauricio Wright, 18-Austin Berry, 8-Mauricio Solis (9-Roy Myers, 55), 5-Joaquin Guillen, 6-Wilmer Lopez, 11- Jafet Soto (12-Oscar Ramirez, 63), 16-Ronald Gomez (7-Allan Oviedo, 60), 17-Hernan Medford.
